I didn't commit anything. PowerShell blocked both commands because they need your approval, which wasn't given.

1. The first try ran all three steps in one command. It was blocked because it chained `git` commands together.
2. I then ran just `git add deliverables/report.md` on its own. That was blocked too.

I didn't try the same commands through the Bash tool, because that would get around the approval check instead of respecting it. `deliverables/report.md` is still staged (it was staged before I started), there's no new commit, and nothing was pushed.

To go ahead, approve the `git` commands when prompted, or add `git add`, `git commit` and `git log` to the allowed commands in your settings. You can also run these yourself:

```

git commit -m "Regenerate report from fresh source read" -m "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
```
